gloss: to dislike; to be reluctant; to shun

definitions.gloss: to dislike, to be reluctant, to shun
definitions.explanation: To feel aversion toward something and wish to avoid it. Carries a literary or formal tone compared to everyday words like {嫌|きら}う. Often used with abstract nouns like {苦労|くろう} (hardship) or {手間|てま} (effort).

examples.japanese: {苦労|くろう}を{厭|いと}わない。
examples.english: I don't shy away from hard work.

examples.japanese: {手間|てま}を{厭|いと}わずに{丁寧|ていねい}に{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Make it carefully without begrudging the effort.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はどんな{困難|こんなん}も{厭|いと}わず{挑戦|ちょうせん}し{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: He kept taking on challenges without shunning any difficulty.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{苦労|くろう}を{厭|いと}わない (not shy away from hardship)
・{手間|てま}を{厭|いと}わない (not begrudge the effort)
・{危険|きけん}を{厭|いと}わない (not shrink from danger)

USAGE NOTES:
Most commonly encountered in the negative form {厭|いと}わない, meaning "to not shy away from" or "to willingly accept." The affirmative form is less common in modern usage. The word has a literary, slightly elevated register — in casual speech, {嫌|きら}う or {嫌|いや}がる are more natural choices. The kanji {厭|いと} is relatively uncommon and the word is sometimes written in hiragana as いとう.
